name: [Equip] Gemini calls are failing
message:
The translation provider is refusing or timing out.

The provider retries transient failures itself (408/429/500/502/503/504, bounded), so this firing means the retries are not clearing it. Translations stop landing; nothing is lost — rows sit at `failed` and the sweep comes back for them — but a course being published now will sit in `publishing`, invisible to students, until it clears.

Where to look:
* `status_code` on the metric separates a rate limit (429) from an outage (5xx) from a network problem (0) from a rejected key (401/403).
* A sustained 429 means the key's quota, not ours: measured 2026-08-17, the key handled 1,626 requests/minute at width 16 without one refusal, so a real 429 storm is a change on Google's side or a runaway loop on ours.

@arvavitcorp@gmail.com

NOTE ON THE QUERY. This used to add two series together — `sum:…{outcome:transport} + sum:…{outcome:retry}` — which reads correctly and does not work: Datadog aligns the two series before adding, so a timestamp present on one side and absent on the other produces no result at all. Both outcomes are rare (4 transport and 3 retry events in the 30 days to 2026-08-19), so in practice the addition would have been empty almost exactly when it mattered. A single query with an OR scope has no such join. `fatal` joined the scope at the same time: a rejected API key produces only fatals, stops every translation dead, and the previous scope could not see it.
